title: OpenAI ChatCompletions proxy: request/response coordinator for streaming + function calls
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a lightweight proxy coordinator that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) requests and responses to Redwood's internal streaming and tool-call surfaces. The coordinator must preserve OpenAI-compatible semantics for request shaping, function_call behavior, and SSE/chunked streaming while leveraging Redwood primitives (prefix caching, token-level telemetry, structured-output enforcement). The goal is zero-code client migration for most OA ChatCompletions users while preventing regressions for Redwood-first features (structured JSON outputs, tool hygiene, stream deltas).
background: Multiple customers ask for an OA-compatible endpoint to reduce porting effort. Existing adapters in the codebase focus on non-streaming or only function-call metadata. This ticket consolidates mappings for: streamed delta events, function_call hints + explicit tool invocations, content-type differences, and error code translations. Previous PRs (ENG-412587, ENG-95321) covered framing and sanitization; this coordinator stitches them together and handles edge cases discovered in canary tests.
tasks: Draft mapping table: OA request fields -> Redwood fields (messages, system role handling, user metadata, function_call options)
Implement request shaper that normalizes role tags and injects idempotency/request-id headers
Stream adapter: convert Redwood token-delta events to OA streaming chunks; support finish_reason variants (stop, length, tool_call) and tool_call multipart signals
Function call flow: translate OA function_call:{name/arguments/auto} into Redwood tool hooks and map tool outputs back to OA function_call.response/arguments
Structured output enforcement: validate JSON schema hints from OA 'function' definitions and apply fallback parsing/repair heuristics
Error surface mapping: map internal runtime errors to OA HTTP codes + descriptive messages
Unit + integration tests including cross-schema property tests and fuzzing for chunk boundaries
Canary rollout plan and rollback hooks with telemetry flags
acceptance_criteria: OA-compliant request sent with sample client (openai-node) receives identical delta stream shape and final JSON payload as from an OA endpoint
Function calls invoked from model are emitted to Redwood tool subsystem and returned to client in OA function_call format
No regression in Redwood-native REST/SDK paths when proxy is enabled (existing test suite green)
Telemetry emits token-level latencies and mapping counters for at least 95% of requests during canary
Security review completed and KMS access scoped for any tool-args persisted

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Chunked JSON in streaming can split a valid JSON token across events, causing consumer parse errors. Mitigation: assemble deltas server-side with low-latency buffer and repair heuristics; expose partial events for debugging.

Risk: Function call semantics differ (OA allows model-initiated tool call with arguments; Redwood tool subsystem expects explicit invocation). Mitigation: add a coordinator layer that transforms model function_call into an internal tool-invoke event and records mapping metadata for replay/observability.
Risk: Increased latency due to extra translation layer. Mitigation: micro-benchmark and apply hot-path optimizations; fallback to pass-through mode for trusted customers.
Risk: Security of arguments stored in logs/telemetry. Mitigation: redact arguments by default, allow opt-in full logging with KMS-backed encryption and access controls.
Risk: Backwards compatibility for clients relying on exact error strings. Mitigation: maintain an error translation table; add header X-OA-Compat-Error for debugging during canary.
Risk: Partial tool outputs in streaming. Mitigation: define canonical finish_reason 'tool' and include tool metadata as OA-compatible final function_call to ease client parsing.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each mapping rule (role, message content, function_call mapping)
Integration test against openai-node SDK: request samples (simple chat, tool-call, streaming JSON payload) and assert identical OA-shaped responses
Fuzz test for chunk boundaries and JSON repair heuristics
Load test to ensure coordinator adds <5ms p50 overhead under expected QPS
Security review tests: verify redaction, KMS flow, and audit logging for tool arguments
rollout_plan: Feature flag: oa_proxy_v1 off by default
Stage 1: internal canary with 5% of internal traffic; monitor mapping error rate and latency
Stage 2: invite-only external canary with selected customers; run A/B against direct Redwood endpoint
Stage 3: broader opt-in with auto-fallback disabled for high-risk accounts
Stage 4: enable-by-default after 2 weeks of stable metrics and security signoff
